st.headline: South Korea denies report on discussing chips as first US investment
st.teaser: A report said the project was facing uncertainty after Washington sought investment in US memory-chip facilities.
fullText: South Korea denied a local media report that the government is discussing a semiconductor project as the first investment under its US$350 billion (S$447 billion) commitment to the US.
A report that the two countries are discussing semiconductors as a candidate for the first strategic investment project “is not true”, the presidential Blue House said in a text message on Aug 18 .
It declined to provide details of talks between Seoul and Washington over the investment pledge.

The statement followed a report by the JoongAng Ilbo newspaper that the first project, which Seoul had aimed to announce later in August , was facing uncertainty after Washington unexpectedly sought investment in US memory-chip facilities.
The US request was a key topic at a closed-door trade meeting held at the Blue House on Aug 13, the newspaper reported, citing unidentified ruling-party officials.
Seoul had initially prioritised the energy sector for its first major US investment, according to the report.

Officials at the meeting largely viewed investment in the US memory-chip facilities as impractical because Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix have already committed to spend at least US$880 billion to build chips and data centres, mainly in South Korea’s southern Honam region, the newspaper said.
Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan arrived in Washington on Aug 16 to resolve last-minute issues over the US investment package.
Kim said detailed practical issues had emerged, but Seoul and Washington were still aiming to finalise talks and announce investment projects as early as late August. Bloomberg

cna.headline: South Korean actor Kim Woo-bin coming to Singapore on Aug 20
cna.teaser: Kim Woo-bin will be in Singapore for the opening of Swiss luxury watchmaker Jaeger-LeCoultre's flagship boutique.
fullText: Popular South Korean actor Kim Woo-bin will be in Singapore this Thursday (Aug 20) to attend the opening of Swiss luxury watchmaker Jaeger-LeCoultre's flagship boutique at Ion Orchard.
The 37-year-old, who is the brand's global ambassador, last appeared in Singapore in 2017 for the premiere of his film Master.
According to Kim's agency, AM Entertainment, the event will take place at 3.50pm at Ion Orchard's atrium on the first level.

View this post on Instagram Kim Woo-bin became a global sensation following his role as the rebellious Choi Young-do in the now-iconic drama The Heirs, which also starred Lee Min-ho and Park Shin-hye.
He recently starred in the Netflix comedy Genie, Make A Wish, which reunited him with actress-singer Bae Suzy.

listening.title: Singapore's Creative Turn to Solar Energy
listening.transcript: Singapore is accelerating its efforts to harness solar energy by installing photovoltaic panels on HDB rooftops across the island. Despite land constraints, the city-state aims to meet at least ten percent of its peak power needs from solar sources by 2030. Industry experts note that while Singapore lacks large open spaces, floating solar farms on reservoirs represent a creative pivot in the nation's energy strategy.

economistArticle.title: The world’s most influential economist is oddly unconvincing
paras: Daron Acemoglu is revered. Having recently secured a Nobel prize, his stature as the world's most influential economist is virtually uncontested. His intellectual corpus, which argues that inclusive institutions drive prosperity while extractive ones breed ruin, has shaped global development policy for decades. Yet, beneath the glittering accolades, a quiet unease lingers among some of his peers. His grand theories, while seductive, can sometimes feel like a beautifully constructed cage that simplifies the chaotic reality of human history.

The core of Acemoglu’s thesis lies in historical determinism, suggesting that early institutional choices lock countries onto rigid pathways. In books like "Why Nations Fail", he and his co-author James Robinson divide the world into neat, digestible binaries. Critics argue that this framework glosses over the messy anomalies that do not fit the paradigm. For instance, the spectacular rise of East Asian economies, including Singapore and China, challenges the simple narrative of democratic inclusivity preceding economic growth.

Indeed, the East Asian miracle suggests that highly centralized, meritocratic bureaucracies can foster immense prosperity without adhering to Western-style democratic norms initially. Acemoglu’s response has often been to categorize these successes as "extractive growth" that is inherently unsustainable. This explanation, however, feels increasingly dogmatic, a convenient way to dismiss empirical evidence that threatens to puncture an elegant intellectual balloon.

Furthermore, his recent focus on technology and artificial intelligence in "Power and Progress" has polarized opinions. He warns that without heavy state intervention, AI will merely enrich tech barons and hollow out the middle class. While his concern for inequality is laudable, his proposed remedies risk stifling the very dynamism that drives technological breakthroughs. To his detractors, he has transitioned from an objective economic historian into an overly prescriptive regulator.

Ultimately, Acemoglu’s influence remains undiminished because he asks the right questions, even if his answers are occasionally unconvincing. He rescued economics from the sterile math of the late twentieth century, returning it to the grand, messy canvas of human history and politics. Whether his grand theory holds up to the complex geopolitics of the twenty-first century remains to be seen, but the debate he has ignited is more vital than ever.
economistArticle.cn:
达龙·阿西莫格鲁深受推崇。在最近获得诺贝尔奖之后，他作为世界上最具影响力的经济学家的地位几乎无可争议。他的学术体系主张包容性制度促进繁荣，而榨取性制度则滋生毁灭，几十年来这一体系一直塑造着全球发展政策。然而，在耀眼的荣誉背后，同行之中却潜藏着一种悄然的不安。他的宏大理论虽然诱人，但有时感觉就像一个建造精美的牢笼，简化了人类历史混乱的现实。

阿西莫格鲁论点的核心在于历史决定论，这表明早期的制度选择会将国家锁在僵化的路径上。在《国家为什么会失败》等著作中，他与合著者詹姆斯·罗宾逊将世界划分为清晰易懂的二元对立。批评者认为，这一框架掩盖了不符合该模式的混乱异常情况。例如，包括新加坡和中国在内的东亚经济体的惊人崛起，就挑战了民主包容性先于经济增长的简单叙事。

事实上，东亚奇迹表明，高度集权、精英治理的官僚机构最初可以在不遵循西方民主规范的情况下促进巨大的繁荣。阿西莫格鲁的反应往往是将这些成功归类为本质上不可持续的“榨取性增长”。然而，这种解释显得越来越教条，成为一种方便地驳斥可能戳破其优雅思想气球的实证证据的手段。

此外，他最近在《权力与进步》中对技术和人工智能的关注两极分化。他警告说，如果没有强有力的国家干预，人工智能只会让科技大亨中饱私囊，并掏空中产阶级。虽然他对不平等的担忧值得赞扬，但他提出的补救措施有窒息推动技术突破的活力的风险。在反对者看来，他已经从一个客观的经济历史学家转变为一个过度指手画脚的监管者。

归根结底，阿西莫格鲁的影响力依然不减，因为他提出了正确的问题，即使他的答案偶尔不令人信服。他将经济学从二十世纪末枯燥的数学中拯救出来，使其重新回到人类历史和政治的宏大而混乱的画布上。他的宏大理论能否经受住二十一世纪复杂地缘政治的考验仍有待观察，但他引发的辩论比以往任何时候都更加至关重要。

gems.s: The core of Acemoglu’s thesis lies in historical determinism, suggesting that early institutional choices lock countries onto rigid pathways.
gems.why: Demonstrates the use of a participle clause ("suggesting that...") to elaborate on the subject ("the core of Acemoglu’s thesis") elegantly and concisely. 演示了如何使用分词短语（"suggesting that..."）来优雅且紧凑地阐述主语。

gems.s: This explanation, however, feels increasingly dogmatic, a convenient way to dismiss empirical evidence that threatens to puncture an elegant intellectual balloon.
gems.why: Uses an appositive noun phrase ("a convenient way to...") to redefine the preceding adjective ("dogmatic"), creating a vivid, metaphorical conclusion. 使用同位语名词短语（"a convenient way to..."）来重新定义前文的形容词，创造了生动且富有比喻色彩的结语。
